ei.title: Chapter 0-QN35 2번: The Risk of Speaking Too Fast
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Speaking fast is a high-risk proposition. It's nearly impossible to maintain the ideal conditions to be persuasive, well-spoken, and effective when the mouth is traveling well over the speed limit. Although we'd like to think that our minds are sharp enough to always make good decisions with the greatest efficiency, they just aren't. In reality, the brain arrives at an intersection of four or five possible things to say and sits idling for a couple of seconds, considering the options. When the brain stops sending navigational instructions back to the mouth and the mouth is moving too fast to pause, that's when you get a verbal fender bender, otherwise known as filler. Um, ah, you know, and like are what your mouth does when it has nowhere to go.

questions.passage: Speaking fast is a high-risk proposition. It's nearly (A)[impossible / possible] to maintain the ideal conditions to be persuasive, well-spoken, and effective when the mouth is traveling well over the speed limit. Although we'd like to think that our minds are (B)[sharp / dull] enough to always make good decisions with the greatest efficiency, they just aren't. In reality, the brain arrives at an intersection of four or five possible things to say and sits idling for a couple of seconds, (C)[ignoring / considering] the options. When the brain stops sending navigational instructions back to the mouth and the mouth is moving too fast to pause, that's when you get a verbal fender bender, otherwise known as filler. Um, ah, you know, and like are what your mouth does when it has nowhere to go.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이상적 조건을 유지하기란 거의 (A)불가능하고... 우리 정신이 충분히 (B)명민하며... 선택지를 (C)고려하며
det.analysis:
❌ ① possible(가능한): (A) 반대 — 빠르게 말하며 이상적 조건 유지는 '불가능(impossible)'
✅ ② impossible — sharp — considering: 원문 조합 ←정답
❌ ③ dull(둔한): (B) 반대 — 우리 정신이 '명민한(sharp)'
❌ ④ ignoring(무시하며): (C) 반대 — 선택지를 '고려하며(considering)'
det.tip: impossible(불가능한) ↔ possible / sharp(명민한) ↔ dull(둔한) / considering(고려하며) ↔ ignoring(무시하며)

In reality, the brain arrives at an intersection of four or five possible things to say and sits idling for a couple of seconds, considering the options. When the brain stops sending navigational instructions back to the mouth and the mouth is moving too fast to (C)[pause / continue], that's when you get a verbal fender bender, otherwise known as filler. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 설득력 있고 말 잘하며 (A)효과적인... 최고의(B) 효율로... 멈출(C) 수 없을 만큼 빠른
det.analysis:
✅ ① effective — greatest — pause: 원문 조합 ←정답
❌ ② useless(쓸모없는): (A) 반대 — 좋은 말하기 자질의 나열이므로 '효과적인(effective)'
❌ ③ least(가장 적은): (B) 반대 — '최고의(greatest)' 효율
❌ ④ continue(계속하다): (C) 반대 — 너무 빨라 '멈출(pause)' 수 없음
det.tip: effective(효과적인) ↔ useless(쓸모없는) / greatest(최고의) ↔ least(가장 적은) / pause(멈추다) ↔ continue(계속하다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이상적 조건을 (A)유지하다... 잠시 (B)공회전하며 멈춰 있다... 뇌가 지시 보내기를 (C)멈추다
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandon(버리다): (A) 반대 — 이상적 조건을 '유지하다(maintain)'
❌ ② rushing(서두르는): (B) 반대 — 뇌가 잠시 '공회전하며(idling)' 멈춰 선택지를 고려함
✅ ③ maintain — idling — stops: 원문 조합 ←정답
❌ ④ continues(계속하다): (C) 반대 — 뇌가 지시 보내기를 '멈출(stops)' 때 필러 발생
det.tip: maintain(유지하다) ↔ abandon(버리다) / idling(공회전하는) ↔ rushing(서두르는) / stop(멈추다) ↔ continue(계속하다)

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 날카로운 — (B) 명민한: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
✅ ② (A) 명민한 — (B) 날카로운: (A)는 '정신이 명민한', (B)는 '칼날이 날카로운' ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 갑작스러운 — (B) 신맛의: 두 문맥 모두에 부적절
❌ ④ (A) 뾰족한 — (B) 급격한: 두 문맥 모두에 부적절
det.tip: sharp: (정신이) 명민한 / (칼이) 날카로운 / (맛이) 신 — 문맥으로 구분

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a point where two or more roads meet and cross each other"

det.korean: 두 개 이상의 도로가 만나 교차하는 지점 = intersection(교차로)
det.analysis:
❌ ① highway(고속도로): 길고 빠른 간선도로로 정의와 다름
❌ ② tunnel(터널): 땅속·산을 관통하는 통로로 정의와 다름
✅ ③ intersection(교차로): 여러 도로가 만나 교차하는 지점 — 정의 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ bridge(다리): 강·계곡 위를 잇는 구조물로 정의와 다름
det.tip: intersection = 교차로. 본문에서 뇌의 선택 지점을 교차로에 비유

questions.passage: Although we'd like to think that our minds are sharp enough to always make good decisions with the greatest efficiency, they just aren't. In reality, the brain arrives at an intersection of four or five possible things to say and sits idling for a couple of seconds, __________ (consider) the options.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 잠시 멈춰 선택지를 고려하면서
det.analysis: 주절(the brain ... sits idling)에 이어지는 분사구문. 주어(the brain)가 동시에 하는 동작을 나타내므로 consider를 현재분사 considering으로 변환. sits idling ..., considering the options = 공회전하며 멈춰 선택지를 고려하면서
det.tip: consider(v. 고려하다) → considering(현재분사, ~하면서). 분사구문

questions.passage: Speaking fast is a high-risk proposition. It's nearly impossible to maintain the ideal conditions to be __________ (persuade), well-spoken, and effective when the mouth is traveling well over the speed limit.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 설득력 있고, 말을 잘하며, 효과적인
det.analysis: 빈칸은 be동사 뒤, well-spoken·effective와 나란히 이어지는 보어 자리이므로 형용사가 필요. 동사 persuade를 형용사 persuasive로 변환. to be persuasive, well-spoken, and effective = 설득력 있고, 말 잘하며, 효과적인
det.tip: persuade(v. 설득하다) → persuasive(adj. 설득력 있는). 형용사 병렬(well-spoken, effective)

questions.passage: Speaking fast is a high-risk proposition. It's nearly impossible to maintain the ideal conditions to be persuasive, well-spoken, and effective when the mouth is traveling well over the speed limit. Although we'd like to think that our minds are sharp enough to always __________ with the greatest efficiency, they just aren't. In reality, the brain arrives at an intersection of four or five possible things to say and sits idling for a couple of seconds, considering the options. When the brain stops sending navigational instructions back to the mouth and the mouth is moving too fast to pause, that's when you get a verbal fender bender, otherwise known as filler. Um, ah, you know, and like are what your mouth does when it has nowhere to go.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리 정신은 최고의 효율로 항상 좋은 결정을 내릴 만큼 명민하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① make good decisions(좋은 결정을 내리다): 명민한 정신이 '효율적으로' 하는 것 — 원문 흐름 ←정답
❌ ② avoid all mistakes(모든 실수를 피하다): 본문에 언급되지 않은 과장
❌ ③ speak very fast(매우 빠르게 말하다): 글은 빠른 말하기를 위험으로 봄 — 반대
❌ ④ waste our time(시간을 낭비하다): 최고의 효율과 정반대
det.tip: sharp enough to make good decisions = 좋은 결정을 내릴 만큼 명민한

questions.passage: Speaking fast is a high-risk proposition. It's nearly impossible to maintain the ideal conditions to be persuasive, well-spoken, and effective when the mouth is traveling well over the speed limit. Although we'd like to think that our minds are sharp enough to always make good decisions with the greatest efficiency, they just aren't. In reality, the brain arrives at an intersection of four or five possible things to say and sits idling for a couple of seconds, considering the options. When the brain stops sending navigational instructions back to the mouth and the mouth is moving too fast to pause, that's when you get a verbal fender bender, otherwise known as filler. Um, ah, you know, and like are what your mouth does when it has __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 입이 갈 곳이 없을 때 하는 것(필러)
det.analysis:
❌ ① too much to say(할 말이 너무 많은): 필러는 할 말을 못 정할 때 나오므로 반대
❌ ② plenty of time(충분한 시간): 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ nothing to fear(두려울 것 없는): 문맥과 무관
✅ ④ nowhere to go(갈 곳이 없는): 뇌가 지시를 멈춰 입이 '갈 곳이 없을' 때 um, ah 같은 필러가 나옴 ←정답
det.tip: what your mouth does when it has nowhere to go = 입이 갈 곳이 없을 때
